description.purpose: One person, as a level. A level owns what its siblings must share, and what two assistants of one person must share is exactly three things: the MEMORY of what was said to that person (memory-hive@3.0.1 -- observations, tagged with the participant set they were learned in, raw and carrying a confidence), the RECORD of who that person and their people are (affinity@3.0.0 -- curated, fail-closed, quotable), and the SCREEN every inbound turn passes (firewall@2.0.4 -- deterministic, row-driven, one rate window). Beside them sits one open container, `assistants`, that the person's agents are instantiated into. The level holds nothing else: no brain, no channel, no tools, no drain, no sink.
description.use_when: One instance per person. A group that owns an agent nobody owns personally is a member too, with its own name -- a group is an AUDIENCE, not a holder, so there is no org-level store to put it in. Instantiate it into an org's `members` container and wire its four inbound and seven outbound lanes in the same mutation; the hive is an island until an edge crosses into it. Assistants come afterwards, one mutation each, instantiated into ./assistants with their own edges to that container. A second assistant for the same person inherits everything this level already knows -- that is the acceptance of GH #122 and the reason the memory is not in the agent.
description.not_in_scope: No agent, no channel, no tool surface: those are the assistant's, and one member may own several. No memory-drain -- per-turn extraction (GH #298, ruling Q11) replaced it, and #302 says explicitly it does not belong in the assistant either. No terminal and no sink of any kind (ruling Q2, GH #284): both refusal lanes leave the level and become no_route in the DLQ if nobody consumes them, which is recorded and self-localising. No second identity store and no org-level memory: 'what does the group know about X' is a filter on the read, never a second store. No push edge into a subscribing brain: a subscribe writes a ROW, never an edge, so the parent draws one edge per subscribing cell -- the recipe is affinity's own, not restated here. No close pass: memory-hive@3.0.1 has an in_close_pass lane, this level does not send it, and whether a close pass should cross the member boundary is a question this template does not answer.
examples: PORTS - the member is an OPEN hive: it declares no params.ports, because it is a level that gets wired INTO and sealing it would refuse exactly the endpoints an assistant instantiation needs. Entry lanes, all four addressed at the member path itself: 'in_turn' -> the screen (promote context.channel, and context.user_id where this colony has per-user firewall rules); 'in_recall' -> this member's memory, turned into the hive's own in_query at the door (send hop.recall_query, hop.memory_tier, hop.recall_window_from, hop.recall_window_to, and the round on context.audience_set + context.channel); 'in_brief' and 'in_propose' -> the record (promote context.asker + context.audience_set for a read, context.actor + context.subscriber for a write). Exits, seven lanes, all leaving the member path: 'answer' (the brief, told apart from a push by hop.subscriber == ''), 'ack' (a write was accepted or rejected), 'reject' (the screen refused a turn, or the memory refused a question or a block), 'error' (a failure that was not a refusal, from a holder OR from an assistant), and the three an assistant raises that nothing here consumes: 'write', 'turn_write', 'prune'. Both refusal lanes MUST be drained by the parent, or they dead-letter as no_route.

the container: ./assistants is a real, empty, open hive. IN: in_turn (the screened turn coming back from the screen) and in_bundle (the memory's answer), both raised by a sibling of the container rather than by a caller outside the member. OUT, the seven of assistant@1.0.0: turn, write, turn_write, extraction, recall, prune, error. The member consumes three itself (turn, recall, extraction) and re-emits the other four on its own contract. The list is derived from templates/assistant/config.json at the tree, and crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh302_member_holds_the_memory.rs reads both files so a lane that moves in the assistant moves here in the same commit.

the unbound behaviour of ./assistants is UNDECLARED, deliberately: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared word could never fire. A message that reaches it before an assistant is instantiated takes the ordinary path. The measurement comes from unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope.

one person, two agents: instantiate member once, then two assistants into ./assistants. The second one starts knowing what the member knows -- same memory, same record, same rate window on the same attacker. Nothing is copied and nothing is synchronised, because there was only ever one of each.

the write half of the memory is one edge: ./assistants -> ./memory-hive on hop.route == 'extraction', re-stamped to in_remember. It is here rather than in the agent because the memory belongs to the MEMBER (GH #122, ADR 0012), and the second edge of talky's two-edge recipe -- the hive's reject egress -- is the ./memory-hive -> . lane this level already ships.
